- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to offset momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently underestimates in early periods of a 30-day forecast (e.g., days 1–5); apply +0.5–1.0% bias to first 5 days.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >1.5% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0%.  
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., +0.6) correlate with 2–3 day price surges; model often misses this; adjust forecast up by 0.5–1.5% for next 2–3 days.
